_what_this_is: The Runpod template for Rigma, in the shape POST /v2/templates accepts.
Every field name and every constraint below was read from the live spec at
https://api.runpod.io/v2/openapi.json while writing this file — nothing here
is inferred from the console or from a blog post.
DEFAULT PATH (no custom image). The template starts from Runpod's own
PyTorch image, which Runpod pre-caches on its hosts, and uses `args` — the
console's 'Container start command' — to run bootstrap.sh, which installs
Rigma and hands over to start.sh. Nothing to build, nothing to push, no
PREBUILT PATH. Build the image in this repo (or let .github/workflows/image.yml
build it), push it, and set `image` to that reference with the same `args`
removed (the image's CMD is already start.sh). Faster and fully pinned.
name: Rigma (LLM agent UI, Vulkan/vLLM)

args: The console's 'Container start command'. The spec accepts either a bare
shell string (treated as CMD and split into arguments) or this JSON form
with explicit entrypoint/cmd. The JSON form is used deliberately: it makes
the shell explicit instead of relying on how a bare string is split.
`exec` matters — this must become PID 1 so a pod stop (SIGTERM) reaches
uvicorn, whose finally block stops the engine.
Omit `args` entirely when using the prebuilt image: its CMD is already
ports: 11500/http is the UI. Runpod proxies a /http port at
https://<pod-id>-11500.proxy.runpod.net — HTTPS only, and it runs through
Cloudflare with a ~100s request cap, so a very long single request can 524.
22/tcp is SSH, which is how you exec into the pod.
PORTS AND ENV ARE SET AT CREATION: neither can be added to a running pod
without a reset. Declare them here.

NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES: UNVERIFIED, AND THE MOST LIKELY THING TO GO WRONG. Rigma's default
backend on an NVIDIA Linux card is Vulkan, and the NVIDIA Vulkan ICD
ships with the HOST driver — it is only mounted into the container when
the container is granted the `graphics` driver capability. No stock
Runpod template sets this (checked against the live catalog: every GPU
template has env {}), so the platform does not do it for you.
start.sh prints the ICD directory and Rigma's own probe result at boot,
so the pod log answers this in the first ten lines. If Vulkan enumerates
nothing, either set RIGMA_ENGINE=vllm with a CUDA image, or
RIGMA_RUNPOD_BACKEND=cpu for a deliberate CPU-only bench.
env.RIGMA_AUTO_CALIBRATE: 0 disables the hardware auto-tune sweep on first load. Set to 1 to let it tune; on a cold volume that adds minutes.
env.RIGMA_MODEL: Empty starts the UI with no model loaded — pick one in the Models tab and it downloads, tunes and loads on demand. Set to a registry slug to download and load on start.
env.RIGMA_ENGINE: llamacpp (Vulkan on NVIDIA Linux) or vllm. vLLM needs RIGMA_MODEL set to a HuggingFace repo id and a non-GGUF model, and refuses rather than falling back.

_field_notes.mounts.persistent: TemplateMounts.persistent is {path,size} in the spec. 100 GB of container disk at /workspace; container disk is wiped when the pod stops.
mounts.network: REJECTED BY THE LIVE API - OBSERVED, NOT INFERRED. Sending any `network`
Both shapes were tried: the object form {"volumeMountPath": "/workspace"}
and the array form [{"volumeId": "..."}] taken from the runpod-migrate
reference. Both were refused with that same message, so `TemplateMounts`
accepts `persistent` only, and `mounts.network` is a POD-creation field
rather than a template field. Attach the volume at POD creation instead
README's deploy steps do. A network volume is DC-locked: the pod must be
created in the same data center.
_field_notes.disk: 20 GB container disk, matching Runpod's own PyTorch template. Rigma's engine is ~30 MiB; models belong on the volume.
_field_notes.allowedCudaVersions: The base image is CUDA 12.4.1, and Runpod's own PyTorch 2.4.0 template allows 12.4-12.9, so this mirrors it. Omit to accept any version.
_field_notes.startJupyter: false: Rigma is the service on this pod, and Jupyter would only add another public port to think about. Set true if you want it — the base image honors the convention, and 8888/http must then be in `ports`.
_field_notes.startSsh: true: sshd is the control channel, and the base image honors the convention. Needs 22/tcp in `ports` (declared above).

_creation_calls.rest_v2: POST https://api.runpod.io/v2/templates with this object (minus the underscore-prefixed keys) and Authorization: Bearer $RUNPOD_API_KEY.
_creation_calls.console: Templates -> New Template, and paste the fields; `args` is the 'Container start command' box.
_creation_calls.note: The underscore-prefixed keys here are documentation. Strip them before sending: the spec's CreateTemplateRequest does not declare them.
